content.text: There are 13 official DnD classes including the Artificer, Barbarian, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Fighter, Monk, Paladin, Ranger, Rogue, Sorcerer, Warlock, and Wizard.
There are also popular 3rd-party classes like the Bloodhunter and the Illrigger, some of which are now available on
. Because there classes are published by other creators, they’re not “official” and your group might not be comfortable using them.

DnD Classes are the mechanical heart of characters in Dungeons and Dragons,
	defining your characters capabilities and role within the party more than any
	other decision point. While your race and background carry equal weight in who
	your character is, your class defines what your character does. Understanding
	how to build and play a class effectively is the most important part of
	building an effective DnD character.

Listed below are Guides on each of DnD’s classes and subclasses, exploring
	the nuances and tricks to get the most out of each. To that end we not only go
	over the features and options of each class, but put those ideas into practice
	with subclass guides and example builds.

We try to keep multiclassing to a minimum in our class and subclass guides,
	but if those advanced options interest you don’t miss our
, both of which go into multiclassing.
This page is primarily focused on the 2014 DnD 5e rules. For the updated, 2014 DnD 5.5 rules see our

sections.heading: What DnD Class Should I Play?

content.text: Choosing your character’s class is arguably the most important decision when building a new character, as it determines their biggest capabilities, their role within the party, and the fantasy that your character will deliver.
If you’re not looking at specific mechanics, it can be helpful to consider what you want your character to do. Some quick suggestions are offered below, but you may also enjoy our

sections.heading: I want to buff my allies

content.text: . The Bard’s Bardic Inspiration feature makes them an easy choice, and that’s available on any Bard subclass.

sections.heading: I want to cast big, explosive spells like Fireball

content.text: . You have a lot of options here, but Sorcerer and Wizard are the go-to.
is an easy choice, allowing you to throw Fireballs and Lightning Bolts without risking friendly fire.
Subclasses for other classes can also work here.

sections.heading: I want to customize my character a lot

content.text: . Each of those classes can provide more decision points than most classes, and you can often change those decisions over time. Artificers get their Infused items, allowing them to craft temporary magic items. Fighters get extra feats. Warlocks get Invocations, allowing them to pick unique features every other level.
Playing a spellcaster is a lot of fun if you like to customize your character a lot, so any class with the Spellcasting feature may be a good choice.

sections.heading: I want to have a pet

content.text: . All four of those subclasses get a pet that can also fight alongside them, each functioning a little differently. For an easy choice, I recommend Drakewarden Ranger.
can animate an object to serve as a temporary pet, but that may not be exactly what you want.
If you want a pet which is more “little buddy” and less “trained attack monster,” you’ll enjoy having a familiar.
can all get familiars right from level 1. Warlocks have unique options to make them even more powerful through their Pact of the Chain feature. Druids can also summon temporary familiars using their

sections.heading: I want to heal my allies

content.text: . All of those options get all of the healing options that you need to restore missing hit points and remove pesky debuffs. If you’re having trouble deciding,
can also heal their allies, but don’t have as much capacity as the other options.

sections.heading: I want to play something easy

content.text: is the simplest character in the game, so it’s great for players looking to jump right into the game.
is an easy choice, but almost all Monks focus on fighting unarmed.

sections.heading: I want to talk to NPCs

content.text: . High Charisma and the right skills (Deception, Intimidation, Persuasion, and sometimes Insight) will help you succeed in social situations.

can also serve as the party’s “Face” thanks to their Expertise feature, allowing them to be unusually good at a few favorite skills. They won’t quite match a Bard, but they’ll do well enough to compete with Paladin, Sorcerer, and Warlock.

sections.heading: I want to sneak through the shadows

content.text: . Pick up skills like Perception and Stealth, and consider proficiency in Thieves’ Tools (Rogues get it for free).
is an easy choice, combining stealth and mobility in an easy package.
built to focus on Dexterity can also be sneaky if you take the right skills. The Criminal Background helps a lot.

sections.heading: I want to swing a big weapon in melee

content.text: . Barbarians will be simplest to play, relying on Rage and Reckless Attack. Fighters will be more tactical, giving you extra feats to customize your tactics. Paladins will be the most survivable, providing both defensive features and healing. If you’re having trouble deciding,

sections.heading: I want to summon creatures to serve me

content.text: can be very powerful and impactful, and each class gets slightly different options. For new players, I strongly recommend the “Summon X” spells introduced in Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything over the “Conjure X” spells in the Player’s Handbook.
Bards and Clerics also get some summoning options, but much later than the other options.
. Each of those options can wear heavy armor and a shield, making them very durable.
. The Druid’s Wild Shape feature allows them to turn into animals, either to sneak around in animal form or to battle enemies. If you want to focus on transforming in combat

sections.heading: I want to use a bow

content.text: . Focus on Dexterity, and get the Archery Fighting Style if it’s an option.
is an easy choice, but almost any type of Ranger is an easy choice as an archer.

sections.heading: I want to use two weapons

content.text: . Two-weapon fighting can be more complicated than most play styles, but it can feel very fun. Most types of Rogues can benefit from fighting with two weapons, but it’s also an iconic tactic for Rangers.

sections.heading: What Classes Do I Need in my Party?

content.text: DnD 5e is resilient enough as a system that a party doesn’t need to adhere to the classic Cleric/Fighter/Rogue/Wizard party makeup, though covering all of those core capabilities can make your party more successful. For a quick, capable party, ensure that someone in the party is filling each of those four “slots.”

If your character’s build won’t neatly fit into those boxes, it may be
	helpful to consider

. Specific roles can be split between the party, and so long as every role is
	represented, your party has everything that it needs to succeed regardless of
	specific classes.

sections.heading: What DnD Class Should I Play First?

content.text:
The Fighter is an easy choice for your first Dungeons & Dragons
	character. Their core mechanics are simple, they’re easy to build, and they’re
	easy to play successfully. Players growing into the game will find points
	within the class which allow you to add more complexity when you feel ready
	for it.

If you want to dive into the game quickly and master the rules quickly, the
	Paladin can be a great choice. They’re more complex than the Fighter, but that
	will expose you to more parts of the rules, allowing you to learn quickly.

But your absolute best choice for your first DnD class is whatever you’re excited to play. If you’re playing a character that doesn’t interest you, it’s difficult to enjoy the game. If you’re playing a character that you’re excited about, even if it’s somewhat complex, you’re going to have more fun with the game and find it easier to learn as you play.

A versatile spellcaster with the ability to create temporary magic items, allowing them to equip and buff both themselves and their party members. Diverse subclasses allow the Artificer to serve a variety of roles ranging from durable front-line melee to powerful ranged damage dealer.

rows.text: Magic items, utility, diverse subclasses to support different playstyles
Partial spellcasting similar to the Wizard

content.text: Choose the Artificer if you enjoy deep customization and the ability to equip a huge number of magic items. In addition to crafting their own temporary items, Artificers are half casters with access to most of the Wizard’s spell list with the addition of crucial healing options and powerful support options.
Your choice of Artificer subclass defines your caacters capabilities and role in the party, making the class very flexible and easy to fit into almost any party.

The 2014 DnD 5e rules include 4 Artificer subclasses. The 2024 DnD 5.5 rules include 6, adding the Cartographer and the Reanimator to the existing options, all of which have been updated to the 5.5 rules.
Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Alchemist: Add new support and healing options, as well as bonus healing and bonus damage with spells which deal certain damage types.
Armorer: Don a suit of magic armor and smash or blast your foes in combat.
Artillerist: Emphasize the Artificer’s abilities as a Blaster, and add the ability to summon magical canons to aid you in combat.
Battle Smith: Focus on fighting with weapons alongside your new Steel Defender, a sturdy pet construct designed for combat.

content.text: The Barbarian is a capable melee warrior who typically thrives using simple, repeatable tactics. Rage allows the Barbarian to be exceptionally durable, allowing you to act aggressively while shrugging off blows that would quickly drop other characters.

rows.text: High risk, high reward play style

content.text: Choose the Barbarian if you want to dive into melee even in the most dangerous situations and walk out victorious.
Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Path of the Ancestral Guardian (2014 only): Conjure up the spirits of your ancestors to defend yourself and your allies in battle.
Path of the Battlerager (2014 only): Spiked armor and an idea of how to make that everyone’s problem.
Path of the Beast (2014 only): Manifest teeth, claws, and other fantastic bodily features, and tear your enemies to shreds.
Path of the Berserker: A disappointing trap for new players in the 2014 rules, but a spectular and simple choice that emphasizes the Barbairan’s core capabilities in the 2024 rules.
Path of the Giant Barbarian (2014 only): Call on the power of the giants to grow in size, hurl items, and deal elemental damage.
Path of the Storm Herald (2014 only): Channel the elemental power of storms to enhance your Rage.
Path of the Totem Warrior: Choose from Animal-themed features, allowing you to customize your barbarian to fill several roles in combat.
Path of the Zealot: Fueled by divine rage, the Zealot is exceptionally difficult to kill and can be raised from the dead without the expensive material components usually required to do so.
Path of Wild Magic (2014 only): Throw unpredictable magic into the mix, gaining a randomly-selected buff every time you rage, allowing you to do fantastic things like teleporting in combat.
Super Mario Jump Attack Build Guide

content.text: A jack of all trades, the Bard falls somewhere between the Rogue’s capability with skills and the Sorcerer’s capabilities with magic. If you want to do a little bit of everything, the Bard is a great choice. With more skills than most characters, Expertise, and full spellcasting, you can build a Bard to fill nearly any roll in your party.

rows.text: Versatile support caster, and useful in any stuation
Excellent skills, especially in social situations
Spellcasting focuses on enchantment and illusion
Bardic Inspiration to buff your allies’ skills and saves
Magical Secrets to learn spells from other classes

content.text: Play a Bard if you want to be useful in every situation, if you’re stuggling to decide on a role within the party, if you love to be the party’s charming face, or if you enjoy supporting your allies to help them succeed.
Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: College of Creation Bard (2014 only): Use the song of creation to sing objects to life or create them out of thing air, and add powerful additional benefits to Bardic Inspiration.

College of Eloquence Bard (2014 only): The best bard that ever did bard, College of Eloquence reinforces and expands upon the Bard’s core class features. While it doesn’t add anything truly new to the class, it does make the Bard’s core features considerably better.
College of Glamour Bard: A combination of support and Charm effects, College of Glamour makes a great support caster but doesn’t add any directly offensive capabilities.
College of Lore Bard: Double down on the Bard’s core features, adding more Expertise, more Magical Secrets, and new support options.
College of Spirits Bard: Commune with the spirits of the dead to empower yourself and your allies and to defeat your enemies.
College of Swords Bard (2014 only): Not just a martial bard, but a
College of Valor Bard: Add some martial capabilities to the Bard, including medium armor, shields, martial weapons, and Extra Attack.
College of Whispers Bard (2014 only): Masters of deceit, infiltration, subterfuge, and psychological warfare.

content.text:
While novice players overlook the Cleric for fear of
	becoming a “healbot”, the Cleric is a much more interesting class than that.
	Diverse, powerful, and backed up by an amazing spell list, clerics can fill a
	variety of roles in the party and support many play styles. They do still have
	the best healing options in the game, but most clerics spend more time
	smashing through fights with Spirit Guardians than they do spamming Cure
	Wounds.

rows.text: Healing, but also durable and dangerous
Powerful spellcasting both defensively and offensively
Bad with weapons (including on subclasses that should be good with weapons)
Use Channel Divinity to turn undead and activate other powerful effects

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Arcana Domain: A magic-focused cleric that worships a deity of magic and borrows a few options from the Wizard.
Death Domain (2014 only): Not all gods of death are about killing things with Necrotic damage, but the subclass sure is.
Forge Domain (2014 only): A front-line, heavily armored cleric with abilities to create items, magically buff their gear, and burn their eemies.
: Straddling the line between life and death, the Grave domain adds a mix of offensive, defensive, and healing options.

Knowledge Domain: Blessed with both magical and mundane knowledge, the Knowledge Domain grants Expertise in two knowledge skills, a number of excellent divination options, and the ability to temporarily gain proficiency in a set of tools.
Life Domain: The iconic healer, but also a strong heavily-armored Defender. Life Domain Clerics are the best healers in the game, but they’re more than just healbots.
Light Domain: Praise the sun, then blast your foes with fire and radiant damage.
Nature Domain (2014 only): The closest you can get to a Druid without being one.
Order Domain (2014 only): A heavily-armored commander, the Order Domain adds great options to lead their allies and enchant their foes in battle.

Peace Domain (2014 only): Nominally themed around a peaceful approach to problems, the Peace Domain offers powerful options to heal and defend your allies, turning them into efficient, resilient, nearly-unstoppable combat monsters.
Tempest Domain (2014 only): Command thunder and lightning to destroy your foes.
Trickery Domain: Skilled in stealth and illusion, the Trickery Domain is welcome among a party or rogues, sneaks, and ne’er-do-wells.
Twilight Domain (2014 only): Use the mystical power of twilight to empower and defend yourself and your allies to overcome any challenge.
War Domain: Direct and simple, the War Domain brings heavy armor, martial weapons, and spells and abilities which allow you to thrive on the front lines of combat.
Home Run Bat: Launching Enemies to Maximum Distance

content.text:
Divine spellcasters with a close bond to nature,
	druids are primarily spellcasters and thrive when controlling their
	environment with area control spells. They match the Cleric’s healing
	capabilities, but present a very different playstyle otherwise. Among their
	most iconic options is Wild Shape, allowing you temporarily adopt the form of
	an animal.

rows.text: Excellent spellcasting for area control and support
Healing magic comparable to the Cleric
Use Wild Shape to turn into animals

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Circle of Dreams (2014 only): A tricky mix of healing, support, and teleportation options.
Circle of Spores (2014 only): A poison-themed master of fungi and mushrooms, you gain the ability to adopt a powerful symbiotic form and to deal huge amounts of poison damage.
Circle of Stars: Draw on the power of magic constellations to change your capabilities, choosing to attack your foes, support and heal your allies, or withstand your foes attacks.
Circle of the Land: Emphasize your connection to the natural with powers related to a favored natural environment.
Circle of the Moon Druid: Master the Druid’s iconic Wild Shape feature, gaining access to more powerful wild shape forms suitable to combat.
Circle of the Shepherd: A powerful summoner with useful abilities to buff and support their allies.
Circle of Wildfire (2014 only): Tame a powerful wildfire spirit which serves you as an ally in combat, and use magic fire to defeat your enemies.

content.text:
Diverse, capable, and effective, the Fighter is an
	iconic warrior. Fighters have many excellent options, and get more Ability
	Score Increases than any other class, allowing them to further customize by
	collecting feats. Because their complexity grows slowly as you level and you
	can add complexity as desired by adding feats, the Fighter is both an easy
	class to play and an exciting class to optimize.

rows.text: Supports a wide variety of play styles
Often struggles to handle large groups of enemies
More ability scores increases and feats than any other class

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Arcane Archer: Imbue arrows with magical effects.
Battle Master: Master of combat maneuvers, the Battle Master uses a unique Maneuvers mechanic which allows you add additional effects to your attacks to harm and hinder your foes.
Cavalier Fighter (2014 only): Known for their exceptional abilities to fight while mounted, but the Cavalier is also a capable bodyguard and Defender.
Champion Fighter: Simple and straightforward, but unquestionably effective, the Champion thrives on the Fighter’s central features.
Echo Knight (2014 only): Summon an echo of yourself from alternate time streams to fight alongside you in combat.
Eldritch Knight: Complement your phenomenal martial prowess with magic to defend yourself and to strike at your foes.
Psi Warrior: Use the power of psionics to boost your attacks, defend yourself and your allies, and mess with your enemies.
Purple Dragon night / Banneret: An inspirational leader and diplomat, the Purple Dragon Knight is a capable leader and good Face despite the stereotypically non-charismatic nature of fighters.
Rune Knight (2014 only): Empower yourself with the magic power of giants, using runes to create fantastic magical effects and enlarging yourself in combat.
Samurai Fighter (2014 only): Capable and resilient, the Samurai is capable of sudden bursts of incredible prowess and adds some proficiencies to aid them in social situations.
Home Run Bat: Launching Enemies to Maximum Distance

content.text:
The iconic unarmed combatant, monks are capable of
	many superheroic physical feats without the use of spells. They’re a comlex
	class to build and play successfully, but their niche between the fighter and
	the rogue can make them a lot of fun. Unfortunately, the mechanical
	requirements of the class mean that monk builds are extremely homogenous and
	there is very little room to deviate without feeling like your character is
	underperforming the rest of your party.

rows.text: Functions well with no weapons or armor

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Way of Mercy: Empower the Monk to harm and afflict your foes and to heal yourself and your allies.
Way of the Ascendant Dragon (2014 only): Breath fire, fly a little bit, maybe frighten your enemies a little bit.
Way of the Astral Self Monk (2014 only): Use your Ki to conjure a magical set of arms and fight using your Ki more than your actual body. (This is the one that’s a Jojo reference.)
Way of the Drunken Master (2014 only): Highly mobile and surprisingly durable.
Way of the Four Elements / Warrior of the Elements: Use the power of the elments to further enhance your martial arts.
Way of the Kensei Monk (2014 only): Master fighting with a weapon.
Way of the Long Death (2014 only) Exceptionally hard to kill, the Way of Long Death allows you to preserve your own life by taking others’.
Way of the Open Hand (2014 only): The master of martial arts, Way of the Open Hand is the simplest and most iconic monk.
Way of the Sun Soul (2014 only): Blast your foes with radiant damage fueled by your Ki.
Super Mario Jump Attack Build Guide

content.text:
Warriors powered by their commitment to a cause,
	the Paladin is nearly always a heavily-armored melee character, equally
	capable of smiting their enemies and healing their allies. Their dependence on
	Charisma also makes them capable in social situations where similar classes
	like the Barbarian and the Fighter often struggle. Because the Paladin’s
	capabilities touch on so many mechanics, Paladins are very mechanically
	satisfying to play and can be a great way to quickly master 5e’s mechanics.
	The Paladin’s Oath will frequently define your flavor and your tactics, but
	usually won’t chnage the core playstyle of the class.

rows.text: Bursts of high damage output with Divine Smite
Aura of Protection provides powerful buffs for yourself and your allies

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Oath of Conquest (2014 only): Use crowd control and defensive options to crush your foes in combat.
Oath of Devotion: The iconic paladin. Defend your allies and smite the wicked.
Oath of Glory: Strive for perfection and glory, making yourself the greatest hero and athlete that you can be.

Oath of Redemption (2014 only): Focused on nonviolent solutions to problems, Oath of Redemption adds spells and abilities to protect yourself and your allies, and to inhibit enemies without harming them.
Oath of the Ancients: Use the power of nature to ensnare and restrain your foes.
Oath of the Crown (2014 only): Force enemies to face you in combat and protect your allies from damage.
Oath of the Watchers (2014 only): Guard the material world against extraplanar foes like elementals, fey, and fiends.

Oath of Vengeance: Focused primarily on Offense, Oath of Vengeance adds powerful new ways to boost your damage output and destroy your foes through force of arms. We like this one so much we accindetally wrote two guides for it!
2014 Oath of Vengeance Paladin Subclass Guide
2014 Oath of Vengeance Paladin Subclass Guide
Oathbreaker (2014 only): A paladin who has broken their oath, the Oathbreaker gainsa evil abilities to harm their foes and to fight alongside undead and fiends.
Hexadin: Suffer Not the Witch-Knight to Live

content.text:
Capable explorers and warriors, the Ranger falls
	somewhere between the Fighter’s martial capabilities, the Rogue’s skills, and
	the Druid’s spellcasting. While early versions of the Ranger struggled
	somewhat due to highly situational class features,

and exciting new subclass options have made the ranger both effective and
	exciting to play.

rows.text: Exploration, good damage output, some utility
Good mix of martial, skills, and spellcasting
Numerous weak class features and bad subclasses
Features to thrive in any environment

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Beast Master: Fight alongside a powerful beast companion, training them as a living weapon to aid you in battle.
Drakewarden (2014 only): Command a powerful drake companion that you can ride into battle!
Fey Wanderer: Gain fey power and use it to beguile, charm, and outwit other creatures.
Gloom Stalker Ranger: Hunt your foes in the dark, gaining the ability to see and fight in the dark, and to ambush your foes.
Horizon Walker (2014 only): Walk the planes, gaining the ability to teleport in battle and to travel between planes without relying on spells like Plane Shift.
Hunter: A capable warrior, the Hunter is the most customizable ranger subclass, capable of succeeding in a variety of fighting styles.
Monster Slayer (2014 only): Simple and reliable; ideal for new players.
Swarmkeeper (2014 only): Use a swarm of fey spirits to empower your attacks, to defend you in combat, and even to carry you through the air.
Home Run Bat: Launching Enemies to Maximum Distance

content.text:
More than just the orphaned thief stereotype, rogues
	are cunning, highly-skilled characters capable of solving many problems and
	filling many roles within a party. The Rogue’s signature combat ability is
	Sneak Attack, which encourages you to use positioning, stealth, and clever
	tactics to deliver powerful single hits.

rows.text: Stealth, sneak attack, and lots of skills
Can fill a variety of skill-based roles in the party
Almost entirely dependent on Sneak Attack to be effective in combat
Cunning Action to make you mobile and sneaky in combat
Sneak Attack for big damage on a single attack

content.text: Choose your ruleset for a complete subclass breakdown:

items.text: Arcane Trickster: Use illusions and enchantments to confuse and outsmart your foes.
Assassin: Masters of infiltration, disguise, and dealing high-damage sneak attacks at the beginning of combat.
Inquisitive (2014 only): Masters of noticing stuff. Perfect in a mystery game.
Mastermind (2014 only): Help your allies in combat, and be very slightly tricky outside of combat.
Phantom: Manipulate the spirits of the dead and use their knowledge to empower your attacks and your skills.
Scout (2014 only): A capable wilderness explorer and ambush leader.
Soulknife: Use psionic power to create deadly psychic blades in combat.
Swashbuckler (2014 only): Charismatic master duelists, swashbucklers use their Charisma in unique ways both in and out of combat, and are masters at engaging foes one-on-one.
Thief: Fast hands, rapid movements, and plenty to do on every turn.

content.text:
Spellcasters that draw their power from something
	innate about themselves, such as draconic ancestry. Sorcerers rely on a small
	number of spells known compared to other spellcasters, but their Metamagic
	feature allows them to customize those spells to suit the needs of their
	situation. Players who enjoy the power of the Wizard but don’t want the
	complexity of managing a spellbook will find the Sorcerer very satisfying.

rows.text: Focus on your favorite spells and adjust them on the fly
Controller, Healer (Divine Soul), Scout, Striker, Support, Utility
Can be simpler to play than the Wizard with much of the same feel
Metamagic can modify spells on the fly
Use Font of Magic to regain spell slots or fuel Metamagic

items.text: Aberrant Mind: Combine the power of psionics with the power of arcane magic to create a spellcaster with the sorcerer’s deep well of spellcasting and some of the warlock’s spooky, occult magic.
Clockwork Soul: An avatar of order, the Clockwork Soul rounds the edges off of probability and wards their allies against harm and entropy.
(2014 only): Descended from a divine bloodline, add the ability to learn and cast cleric spells in addition to sorcerer spells. 2014 Guide
: Extra durable and extra excited about dragons and elemental damage. 2014 Guide | 2024 Guide
(2014 only): Change your subclass spells by changing phases of the moon, and also get discounts on Sorcery Points. 2014 Guide
: Masters of magical darkness, gain the ability to see in darkness and summon a powerful shadow hound to weaken and attack your foes. 2014 Guide

(2014 only): Adept at flight and casting spells in close quarters, storm sorcerers dart in and out of close range to deal bursts of sonic and lightning damage before flying back out of reach and retreating. 2014 Guide
: Wacky chaos monsters but also powerful rerolls and the ability to mess with dice math. 2014 Guide | 2024 Guide

content.text:
Warlocks draw their power from a pact made with a
	powerful entity of some kind known as your “Patron,” who provides you with
	magical secrets to magical power. Mechanically, the Warlock is delightfully
	weird compared to other options, offering a huge number of customization
	points and entirely unique spellcasting mechanic that makes them feel and play
	very differently from other spellcasters. Building around Eldritch Blast has
	been simple and effective since the Player’s Guide released in 2014, but that
	is certainly not the only way to build an effective Warlock.

rows.text: Exclusive access to Eldritch Blast, the best offensive cantrip in the game

items.text: Archfey: Fey are tricky, unpredictable creatures, and warlocks who chooses an archfey patron gain spells and abilities to confuse, surprise, and charm other creatures.
Celestial: Choose a patron from the upper plains and some healing and radiant damage to your capabilities.

Fathomless (2014 only): A powerful threat in and around water, the Fathomless patron gives you new spells related to storms and water, and you gain the ability to conjure spectral tentacles to attack your foes and to defend you from harm.
Fiend (2014 only): Choose a fiending patron and get all of the fire damage you could even possibly want. Other stuff, too, but Fireball is pretty great.

Genie (2014 only): Choose a genie patrong from one of the four major elements, and gain benefits like empowered spellcasting and a magic vessel which you can use both as a spellcasting focus and as a resting place.
Great Old One: Make a pact with a cosmic horror Patron gain spooky spells, telepathy, and
Hexblade (2014 only): Forge a pact with a mystical force known only as “The Hexblade”, gaining the ability to use Charisma for weapon attacks and other fantastic combat abilities.
Undead (2014 only): Gain the ability to adopt a terrifying undead visage to buff yourself in combat.
Undying (2014 only): Make a pact with an immortal (or at least very long-lived) patron and become very slightly less likely to die.
Hexadin: Suffer Not the Witch-Knight to Live

content.text:
Among the most iconic spellcasters in D&D, the
	Wizard is your iconic book-bearing magical scholar. Their spell list is the
	largest in the game and includes many of the best spells in the game, plus
	their ability to collect spells and cast any ritual that they know makes the
	Wizard an excellent utility caster on top of their ability to hurl
	fireballs.

rows.text: A spell to solve every problem
Poor (but can be imporved with the right spells)
Biggest spell list in the game, covering every capability except healing
Can cast rituals from their spellbook without preparing them

items.text: Bladesinging / Bladesinger: Masters of fighting with both weapons and with spells, bladesingers can perform a secret song and dance which makes them deadly in combat. Among the most caster-focused gish options.

Chronurgy Magic (2014 only): Manipulate the flow of time, allowing you to force rerolls, to stop creatures, and even to temporarily suspend spells in a tiny bead and share it with your allies. Chronurgists also gain access to the Dunamancy spell list.

Graviturgy Magic (2014 only): Manipulate space and gravity to move your foes about on the battlefield and crush them with powerful gravitational effects. Graviturgists also gain access to the Dunamancy spell list.
Order of Scribes (2014 only): Awaken your spellbook, and master the central concepts of wizardly magic, allowing you to learn spells faster than other wizards and employ them in new and unusual ways.
School of Abjuration / Abjurer: Masters of protective magic, Abjurers gain a powerful magical ward which can absorb damage dealt to you or your allies and recharges when you cast abjuration spells.
School of Conjuration / Conjurer: Conjuration covers both teleportation and summoning, and Conjurers are build to be good at both.

School of Divination / Diviner: Diviners gain the powerful Portent feature, allowing them to roll two to three d20’s at the beginning of the day and use them to replace rolls, as well as the ability to cast divination spells and incredible little cost.
School of Enchantment / Enchanter: Powerful and versatile spellcasters, enchanters gain abilities to charm and hypnotize foes, and to affect additional targets with single-target enchantment spells.

School of Evocation / Evoker: Exceptional at dealing damage with spells, evokers deal more damage with cantrips than other spellcaster, and can make safe spaces in their area damage spells to avoid harming allies.
School of Illusion / Illusionist: Masters of illusion spells, illusionists gain abilities to manipulate illusion spells beyond their normal limits, including the ability to make them partially real.

School of Necromancy / Necromancer: Gain the ability to heal yourself when you kill other creatures, and to more easily create and control undead, including powerful ones far more powerful than spells alone would allow.

School of Transmutation / Transmuter: Gain abilities to turn things into other things, like wood into metal, yourself into an animal, dead things into live things, and injured or sick things into happy and healthy things.
War Magic (2014 only): Powerful combatants, war wizards gain abilities to defend themselves against attacks and to boost their spell damage by countering or dispelling other spells.

If your group wants to explore 3rd-party content, we hope that these articles will help you make them work for you.

sections.heading: Does my DnD party always need a cleric?

content.text: No! While it’s helpful to include a healer in the party, the Cleric isn’t your only option. Bards and Druids have similar healing capabilities to the Cleric, and Artificers, Way of Mercy Monks, Paladins, and Rangers can all provide healing (thought not as good as the Clerics).

sections.heading: What are the easiest DnD classes to play?

content.text: The Barbarian, Fighter, Rogue, and Warlock are easy to play compared to other DnD classes.

sections.heading: What is the best DnD class in DnD 5e?

content.text: The Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, and Wizard are typically considered the most powerful DnD classes. However, it’s generally best to consider what class is best for what you want to do.
Best stealth: Bard, Druid, Ranger, Rogue
Best support: Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard

sections.heading: What is the best DnD class for a new player in DnD 5e?

content.text: Mechanically simple classes like the Fighter and Rogue are easy for new players to learn. If you want a spellcaster, the Wizard is easy learn and grows in power as you learn the game more. If you want to learn the game thoroughly, the Paladin interacts with many of the game’s mechanics and they’re notoriously difficult to kill.

content.text: In the 2014 DnD 5e rules, the Monk and the Ranger are considered the worst classes.

sections.heading: What are the hardest DnD Classes to play in DnD 5e?

content.text: The Monk and the Ranger are among the most difficult classes to play successfully. The Druid can also be complex to master becuase it has so many complicated features.
